name: Outstation – Taxi & Cab Booking for WooCommerce
author: webowns

sections.description:
Outstation turns your WordPress site into a complete taxi and cab booking website, like the big travel apps: outstation one-way and round trips, airport transfers, hourly rentals and city taxis. Customers search, compare cabs with real fares, pay online with any WooCommerce payment gateway and manage their trips. You run cars, drivers, prices, bookings and SEO pages from one simple admin.

Built for taxi operators, travel agencies and car rental companies in any country. Mobile-first, works with any theme (best with Astra, also with block themes such as Twenty Twenty-Five).

For your customers

  • Search like a travel app: one-way, round trip, airport transfer and hourly rental, with stops, date and time pickers and Google address search.
  • Phone address picker: full screen, with “Use current location”, recent places, your own cities and airports, and a map pin for the exact pickup point (the driver gets a navigation link to it).
  • Results with real fares: car photo, fuel, seats, AC, taxes and tolls shown clearly; sort and filter by price, car type and fuel.
  • Review and pay in two app-style steps: itinerary, what is included, extra charges and traveller details, with part pay or full pay.
  • Any WooCommerce payment gateway: Stripe, PayPal, Razorpay, PayU, Cashfree, cash and more.
  • Pay the balance later: pay the rest online from My trips or from a link sent by you or the driver, or pay the driver in cash.
  • My trips: sign in or sign up popup with your logo, upcoming and past trips, trip codes, driver details, payment history, invoices and cancellation. Guests find a booking with its ID and phone.
  • Help and complaints: one support chat per booking, with email notifications on both sides.
  • Genuine reviews: a “Rate your trip” email after the trip; approved reviews show on city and route pages with star ratings for Google.
  • Extras: trip add-ons (roof carrier, child seat…), booking window and minimum notice, whole-amount fares, a callback form and an optional “Call me back” button.

For you and your team

  • Setup wizard: installs WooCommerce and Astra, sets currency, tax and phone code for your country, adds your logo and creates all pages, the menu and sample cars.
  • Bookings: filter by date and status, search, CSV export, phone and WhatsApp bookings with the fare calculated for you, and edit any booking.
  • Booking detail screen: Google Maps links, call and WhatsApp buttons, ready WhatsApp messages, payment link, payment history, trip codes, timeline, and change the car, the driver or both with a reason.
  • Driver app on the phone: a full-screen page with Trips, History and Profile. Drivers sign in with email or mobile and password (emailed when you add them), navigate, call the customer, send a payment link, and start and end the trip with the customer’s codes.
  • Trip codes (OTP): a start code and an end code, so no trip is marked done without the customer.
  • Auto-assign (optional): a free car and driver for each new booking; no car or driver gets two trips at once.
  • No double bookings: a car is busy for every day of its trip, checked again at checkout.
  • Fleet: cars, models, brands, categories, price groups and service areas drawn on the map; one card per model (“Dzire or similar”).
  • Customers, reports and staff: customer history and “Log in as customer”, trips and money per driver and per car, and staff logins (Cab Manager, Dispatcher) that see only what they need.
  • Automatic emails: booking confirmed, driver assigned, cancelled, welcome and reminder, with your branding, preview and test.
  • Invoices: tax invoices with your tax name and number (GST, VAT…); print or save as PDF.

Fares and pricing

  • One server-side fare engine for search, cab page and checkout; prices sent by the browser are never trusted.
  • Base fare, base km, rate per km (AC / non-AC), minimum fare and night charge per car type and fuel.
  • Round trips with minimum km and driver allowance per day; hourly rentals with km per hour and minimum hours.
  • Tax with your own name and rate, convenience fee, online discount, waiting charges, tolls included or extra.

Google Maps, with a small bill

  • Key check: paste your key and see which Google APIs work and which to enable, with a step-by-step guide.
  • Switches for address suggestions, “Use current location”, the map pin and traffic-aware distances. Fares work with all of them off.
  • Fewer paid requests: suggestions after 3 letters and a pause in typing, nothing paid twice in a visit, and server-side caching of every address and distance.
  • An optional server key, so the key in your pages can be locked to your website.

SEO pages that bring bookings

  • City taxi, airport cab and route pages (such as “Bhopal to Indore cab”) with fares for every car, FAQ and structured data.
  • Canonical URLs, meta descriptions, Open Graph tags, breadcrumbs and a sitemap (works with Yoast SEO and Rank Math).
  • Add many routes at once, edit each page’s text, FAQ and sections, and show or hide pages.

Built the WordPress way

  • Every screen is a shortcode on a normal page, so any page builder works around it.
  • Translation-ready, with privacy tools (export and erase personal data) and optional data removal on uninstall.
  • Anonymous usage statistics only if you agree in the setup wizard (see External Services).

Support and custom development

Need help or a custom feature for your cab business? Ask in the support forum or message the developer on WhatsApp: +91 74705 26894.

External Services

The plugin connects to these third-party services:

Google Maps Platform

  • When: the booking form loads Google Maps for address suggestions and the map pin; the server looks up addresses (Geocoding API) and road distances (Routes API or Directions API) to calculate fares; the key check in Settings tests the key when you paste it.
  • Data sent: place names, addresses and map coordinates. No names, phone numbers or emails.
  • Terms · Privacy policy

Razorpay (only if you use it)

  • When: at checkout, when the customer pays with Razorpay.
  • Data sent: order number, amount, currency and the customer’s name, email and phone, to create and verify the payment.
  • Terms · Privacy policy

WordPress.org (setup wizard only)

  • When: only when you click “Install” for WooCommerce or Astra; the standard WordPress download, as in Plugins > Add New. No booking or customer data.
  • Privacy policy

WhatsApp links

  • When: never automatically. Buttons such as “Chat with us” or “WhatsApp driver” open WhatsApp only when clicked, with the message text in the link (trip details, names and phone numbers for admin buttons).
  • Terms · Privacy policy

WP Track by Mapthrust (only if you opt in)

  • When: only if you click “Allow” in the setup wizard or in Settings; “No thanks” works fully, and turning it off deletes your site’s record. Sent on activation, a weekly check-in, update, deactivation (reason only if you give one) and deletion.
  • Data sent: site address and title; plugin, WordPress, PHP, WooCommerce and database versions; language, time zone, country, theme, multisite; server details (web server, PHP limits and extensions, HTTPS, currency); active plugins; which Outstation features are on (never keys); totals of cars, bookings, drivers and service areas, and monthly booking values; and errors in Outstation’s own files.
  • Your email and name only if you also tick the separate updates box (unticked by default). Never passwords, API keys or customer details.
  • Service · Terms and privacy policy

OpenStreetMap Nominatim (admin only)

  • When: only when an administrator clicks “Draw boundary” on the Service areas screen.
  • Data sent: the place name typed in the Location field. No customer data.
  • Usage policy · Privacy policy · Data © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL

Privacy Policy

The plugin stores bookings in your WordPress database: traveller names, phone numbers, emails, pickup and drop locations, dates, times and payment transaction IDs.

  • Locations are sent to Google Maps to calculate distances; payment details go to your payment gateway (see External Services).
  • A customer who rates a trip chooses the name shown with the review; you can hide or delete any review.
  • Cookies: when a customer signs in, signs up or books, a random session cookie (wpcab_user_id) keeps them signed in for 30 days. It holds no personal data. Visitors who only browse get no plugin cookie.
sections.installation:
Minimum Requirements

  • WordPress 5.0 or higher
  • PHP 7.4 or higher
  • WooCommerce 8.0 or higher (installed and active)

Installation Steps

  1. Upload the outstation-by-webowns directory to your /wp-content/plugins/ directory, or upload the ZIP file directly via the WordPress admin dashboard (‘Plugins’ > ‘Add New’ > ‘Upload’).
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ menu in WordPress.
  3. Once activated, go to the Outstation menu in your WordPress sidebar.
  4. Run the Setup wizard (Outstation > Settings > Setup wizard): it creates the pages, menu and sample cars. Then add your Google Maps key in Settings > Integrations; the key check shows which Google APIs to enable.
  5. Save your settings. If you receive a warning about pretty permalinks, ensure they are enabled under Settings > Permalinks (e.g., Post name structure) and flush the rewrite rules on the dashboard notice.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin require WooCommerce?

Yes. The plugin utilizes WooCommerce to manage checkout, payment gateways, tax calculation, and order tracking. WooCommerce must be installed and activated for booking functionality.

How do I display the booking form on my site?

You can display the booking form on any page or post using the shortcode [wpcab_booking]. By default, it displays the full search form.

Which payment gateways are supported?

Since the booking process is integrated with WooCommerce, you can use any payment gateway supported by WooCommerce, including Stripe, PayPal, Cash on Delivery (COD), and direct bank transfers. The plugin also includes custom checkout optimizations specifically tailored for Razorpay.

Which theme should I use?

Outstation works with any theme, but we recommend the free Astra theme. When Astra is active, the plugin automatically gives its booking pages a full-width layout without sidebars or page titles, and adds the customer Login/Signup button to the header menu. To turn off the header button, add add_filter( 'wpcab_astra_header_account', '__return_false' ); to your theme’s functions.php.

Which Google Maps APIs do I need?

Maps JavaScript API, Places API, Geocoding API and Directions API (the Routes API is optional). Paste your key in Settings > Integrations and the key check tells you which ones are missing, with a link to enable each. A step-by-step guide is right below it.

How do drivers use it?

Add the driver with an email address and they get their sign-in and a first password by email. They open the Driver page on their phone (it works like an app, with Trips, History and Profile), and can add it to the home screen. You can also send them a private link on WhatsApp from the Drivers screen.

How is the trip distance calculated?

The plugin uses the Google Routes API v2 (with a fallback to the Google Maps Directions API) to calculate the exact driving distance between the pickup and drop-off locations, which is then used to compute fare pricing dynamically.

What is Geofencing and how does it work?

Geofencing allows you to define geographical boundaries (Circles or Polygons) on a map. When a customer enters a pickup location on the booking form, the plugin checks if it falls within any active geofences and only shows vehicles that are assigned to those geofences or marked as global.

How do I set up SEO-friendly route pages?

Navigate to Outstation > City & Route Pages. Here, you can generate customized pages for specific routes (e.g., “Delhi to Jaipur”), set custom meta descriptions, and manage rewrite rules for pretty URLs.
sections.changelog:
3.5

  • New: on the booking screen, change the car, the driver or both. The car’s own driver comes with it automatically (untick to keep the current driver), or change only the driver. Pick a reason (car breakdown, driver not available, driver late, customer request, upgrade or your own note); every change shows in the timeline with who made it and when.
  • New: a warning when the new car or driver already has another trip at that time; the cab type follows the new car, and the old car and driver are freed when they have no other trip.
  • Fixed: a background email step no longer fails when WordPress stops loading early.

3.4

  • New: the driver page is a full-screen app on the phone, without the website header, menus or footer, with a bottom menu: Trips (current and upcoming, with a count), History and Profile (contact, call the office, change password, sign out).
  • New: a new driver with an email address gets their sign-in and a first password by email; “Forgot password?” works for every driver.
  • Fixed: on phones, searching for a new address after opening the map now closes the map and shows the suggestions.
  • Changed: cleaner spacing and sizes on the search form and results (one gap between cab cards, filters aligned with the results, readable labels), one price format everywhere, the route shown above the results, and no emoji or exclamation marks in customer emails.
  • Changed: the “Call me back” button stays off unless you switch it on in Settings > Customer features.

3.3

  • New: Google Maps key check (Settings > Integrations). It runs by itself when you paste a key and tests every Google API the plugin needs from your server (Geocoding, Directions, Routes) and from the browser (Maps JavaScript, Places, Geocoding), says which ones are not enabled and why (wrong key, no billing, website or IP restriction), with an “Enable” button for each.
  • New: step-by-step guide to create the key, enable the APIs, protect the key and set a daily limit.
  • Changed: the second key field is now “Server key (optional)”. When set, all lookups your server makes use it, so the browser key can be locked to your website. Empty: the browser key is used for both, as before.

3.2

  • New: Google Maps usage (Settings > Integrations). Switch each paid Google feature on or off: address suggestions while typing, “Use current location”, “Set location on map” pin, live distance on the classic booking form and traffic-aware distances. Fares keep working with any of them off.
  • New: suggestions start after a chosen number of letters (3 by default) and wait for a short pause in typing, so typing an address sends one or two requests instead of one per letter.
  • New: the same search, place, address or route is not paid twice in a visit (browser cache), place details ask only for basic fields, and the server caches every address and distance (failed lookups are retried after an hour instead of a month).
  • New: monthly table of the requests your server sent to Google.
  • Changed: distances use the cheaper route request unless “Traffic-aware distances” is on; when the Routes API is not enabled for your key the plugin goes straight to the Directions API instead of trying Routes first on every search.
  • Changed: the live distance preview on the classic [wpcab_booking] form is off by default (the fare page shows the distance).

3.1

  • New: booking detail screen (click a booking): trip with Google Maps links, customer and driver with call and WhatsApp, ready WhatsApp messages (booking details, driver details, pickup reminder, payment due, trip code, trip sheet, collect payment, pickup location), exactly what the driver collects, trip codes, timeline, and status and driver changes.
  • New: edit any booking (route, date and time, cab, driver, fare, payment, traveller, notes), with the option to email the updated details.
  • New: add, edit and delete customers (their bookings are kept).
  • New: pay the balance online later. Each booking has a payment link: “Pay online now” in My trips and on the confirmation page; admins email, WhatsApp or copy it; drivers send it from their panel. When paid it is added to the booking automatically, so the driver collects nothing. Cash still works as before.
  • New: staff logins. Roles “Cab Manager” (bookings, customers, support, fleet, drivers, pages) and “Dispatcher” (bookings, customers, support) see only their part of Outstation; Settings > Staff explains them and lists your team.
  • New: “Forgot password?” by email for customers (login popup) and drivers (driver sign-in). Single-use link, valid for an hour.
  • New: each city, airport and route page has its own heading, intro line, Google description, questions and answers, and which sections to show, set in the page’s editor (Pages & SEO > City & route pages). Empty fields use the common text.
  • Improved: Settings split into clear tabs: Bookings, Fares & payments, Trip types & charges, Drivers & trips, Customer features, Business & invoices, Emails, Integrations, Appearance, Staff, Data & privacy.
  • Improved: the “Book a cab” page is no longer required (the home page search box does the same); the Setup guide points to the wizard, which creates every page.
  • New: payment history on every booking (admin and My trips): each payment with date, method, transaction ID and amount: the online payment, balances paid online later, cash collected by the driver and balances marked collected by the office.
  • Improved: works the same in any country. Prices always use your store currency (the city and airport pages no longer convert fares with a fixed rupee rate), address and distance lookups use your business country instead of always adding “India”, any country’s mobile numbers are accepted, the phone code defaults to your store country, the location suggestions are your own cities, drivers’ ID document is optional and generic, and wording such as UPI, GST and Aadhaar is gone outside India.
  • Changed: the Book a cab page no longer shows a long built-in text; it shows a short, translatable FAQ based on your settings.
  • Fixed: signing in from the popup shown while booking did nothing.
  • Fixed: on Help & support, “Get help with this trip” opened the login popup for signed-in customers.
  • Fixed: desktop home page search box touched the header.

3.0

  • Improved: Pay & Confirm is up to 3 times faster (no map lookups while placing the order; background emails start instantly).
  • New: loading bar at the top of the screen and a spinner on the tapped button, so customers see that a search, a cab, Pay or sign-in is loading.
  • New: Customers has its own entry in the Outstation menu (each customer’s bookings, value and payments).
  • Improved: Setup page lists your site page by page (Home, Book a cab, Search results, Cab details, routes, city, airport, My trips, Help, Driver) with a green tick or “Create page”, how to create it yourself, and a large desktop/phone preview of exactly what each shortcode shows. The old long guide is gone.
  • Fixed: the close (X) button of the full-size car photo did not work.

2.9

  • New: drivers can sign in to the driver panel with email or mobile number and a password (set by you in Drivers, or by the driver in the panel), see their full trip history and sign out. The private link still works.

  • New: Call driver and WhatsApp buttons on the customer’s booking; the driver panel already calls the customer.

  • Changed: Freemius removed (no more opt-in screen after activation and no email address is ever asked for).
  • New: optional “Help improve Outstation” step at the end of the setup wizard. If you click Allow, only your site address and technical details are shared (see External services); turn it on or off in Settings > Booking. Turning it off deletes your site’s record.
  • New: when sharing is on, deactivating the plugin asks an optional reason (Skip is always there).
  • Changed: clean-up on delete runs from uninstall.php again (same behaviour: data is only removed when “Delete all data when the plugin is deleted” is ticked).

  • New: optional opt-in (Freemius) for security and feature update emails and basic, non-sensitive usage data. Nothing is shared unless you click “Allow & Continue”; “Skip” keeps everything working. See External Services.

Drivers > “Panel link” sends a private link on WhatsApp; the driver sees today’s and upcoming trips, navigates to the pickup, calls or messages the customer and marks the trip completed (optionally with the balance collected in cash). Resetting the link signs that phone out.
  • New: Fleet & Prices > Reports: trips, completed, booking value and money received for every driver and car, and each one’s trip list.
  • New: Service areas > “Draw boundary”: type a city or area and its real border is drawn (OpenStreetMap), ready to adjust. The drawing buttons now always show (they could be missing in the popup).
  • New: results show one card per car model, using a free car of that model; at checkout a taken car is swapped for another free car of the same model.
  • Improved: money paid online is stored on the booking, so “still to pay” and reports are right without opening the order (earlier bookings are filled in once).
  • Tested with 500 cars and 18,000 bookings.

2.5

  • Fix: availability ignored paid bookings (status “processing” or “on hold”), so a booked car could be booked again for the same day.
  • Fix: on city and airport pages a car with any confirmed booking, on any date, was shown as unavailable for ever.
  • New: multi-day round trips block the car on every day of the trip (bookings now store the return date); airport and hourly trips only block overlapping times; checkout checks again before payment.
  • New: faster results with many cars (one availability query per search instead of one per car) and database indexes for busy sites.
  • New: New booking screen finds returning customers by phone or email and suggests addresses for pickup and drop.
  • New: Settings > Setup is a short checklist with “Set up everything automatically”; the manual guide moved under Advanced.
  • Fix: the Customers list could show only one row (sorting error on some MySQL / MariaDB versions).
  • Improved: tighter sign in / sign up popup; the “Call me back” button stays behind popups.

2.4

  • New: Settings > Booking > Trip types & charges: offer or hide one way, round trip, airport transfer and hourly rental; per type set tolls and parking (included or extra), free waiting minutes, waiting per hour and the extra-hour rate for rentals. Hidden types disappear from every search form and are refused by the server.
  • New: the price note on results and the extra charges on the cab page follow the trip type (for example free waiting after the flight lands for airport pickups, waiting included in the hours for rentals).
  • New: optional “Call me back” popup (Settings > Booking > Callback popup): a floating button or a sheet that opens by itself once per visit; requests go to Support > Callback requests.
  • Fix: the extra line on result cards squeezed the desktop card layout.

  • Fix: checkout failed with an error page for a customer whose account was created from a phone booking (no password yet). They now set a password with the mobile number on file.
  • Fix: the “Booking confirmed” email could be sent twice; WooCommerce’s own customer order emails no longer repeat the plugin’s booking emails for cab orders.
  • Fix: changes to a car (price, status, service area) took up to 4 hours to show on the site.
  • Fix: “My Bookings” in the menu opened the WooCommerce account page (customers have no WordPress login).
  • New: My trips page ([wpcab_my_account]) with upcoming, completed and cancelled trips, booking details, invoice, help, rating and cancel; “Find my booking” for guests.
  • New: Help & support page ([wpcab_help]): choose a trip to report a problem and see all complaints with their status and replies. Added to the menu.
  • New: booking confirmation page after payment with the trip, amounts paid and due, payment instructions and invoice download.
  • New: Bookings > Customers with trips, booking value, paid amount and history; “Log in as customer” for admins.
  • New: Support menu (tickets, callback requests, reviews) with a count of items waiting.
  • New: service areas now limit which cars appear on the results and route pages and are checked again at checkout.
  • New: a pickup that is only a city must be pinned on the map or typed as an exact address before payment.
  • New: booking the same trip twice (same customer, pickup, date and time) asks first.
  • New: “Inclusions & policies” sheet on the cab page, with cancellation, luggage and other rules editable in Settings > Booking > Trip policies.
  • New: {tax_label} email placeholder: tax is shown with your own name and rate (GST, VAT, sales tax…) instead of a fixed “GST”.
  • New: failed emails are retried automatically (up to two more tries).
  • Improved: search form, results cards (km included, extra km rate, bags), checkout on phones, account menu, links above the footer grouped by city.

2.2

One review per completed trip, approved in Bookings > Reviews (optionally publish 4-5 star reviews automatically).
  • New: city, route and airport pages show the average rating and recent reviews, and add the rating to their structured data once the page has enough of its own reviews (Settings > Booking > Customer reviews). Shortcode [wpcab_reviews].
  • New: on phones, choosing an exact address in the address picker opens a map with a centre pin to set the precise point; “Set location on map” and “Use current location” open it too. The confirmed pickup point is reused on the cab page.
  • Fix: brands and price groups that are still used by models or vehicles could be deleted (the check failed); categories had no check at all.
  • Fix: editing a price group could clear all its fares if the page script did not load.
  • Fix: adding a vehicle silently required RC, insurance and owner ID files; they are now optional (vehicle photos are still required).

  • Fix: fuel type matching for vehicle prices is no longer case sensitive.

2.1

  • Fix: searching on a new phone or browser could show “No vehicles available”: the search was not saved. The search now also travels in the page address, so refresh and shared links keep the trip.
  • Fix: city, route and airport pages told search engines they were copies of one page (wrong canonical URL). Each page now has its own canonical URL, meta description and share (Open Graph / Twitter) tags; Yoast SEO and Rank Math get the same values.
  • New: sitemap of every city, route and airport page, in the WordPress sitemap and at /wpcab-sitemap.xml (added to the Yoast SEO and Rank Math sitemap index and robots.txt).
  • New: breadcrumb structured data and the real fare range (cheapest to costliest cab) in the TaxiService data on route pages.
  • New: results on phones work like a travel app: chips for Filters and car types, compact cards, tap a card to choose it, cheapest cab first and booked cabs last.
  • New: “Round fares to whole amounts” setting (on by default): no decimals, and the price shown is exactly the amount charged.
  • New: “Book up to (days ahead)” and minimum notice now grey out dates in every calendar, not only at checkout.
  • New: when no pickup time (or a time that has passed) is given, results show the next available time instead of an empty list.
  • New: the best image size is shown under every image upload (vehicle photos, brand logos, driver photos), with a warning when a picture is too small.

  • Fix: car photos broke when the site was opened on another address or moved to a new domain.

  • Fixed: a booking refused for a past pickup time lost the trip details; the cab page now warns early and lets the customer pick a new time.
  • Fixed: “View details” in My Bookings did not work for customers.

  • Fixed: service area drawing stopped working after Google removed its drawing tool; a new Circle/Area toolbar replaces it.
  • Fixed: booking statuses could put WooCommerce orders into an invalid status; statuses are now validated.
  • Fixed: times in some emails and messages could be shifted by the site time zone.
  • Fixed: setting the site time zone from the country in the Setup Wizard.

1.9

  • New: one-time Setup Wizard after activation: installs WooCommerce and the Astra theme, sets currency, tax name and rate and phone code for your country, adds your logo and business details, creates the shortcode pages, header menu, Terms & Conditions and Cancellation Policy pages, and optional sample cars and routes.
  • New: invoices (tax invoice with GSTIN and CGST/SGST in India, VAT elsewhere) that customers open from My Bookings and admins from Bookings; print or save as PDF.
  • New: paid / due amounts on every booking and “Mark paid” when the driver collects the balance.
  • New: “Request a callback” form on city, airport and route pages ([wpcab_callback_form] shortcode), with a Callback Requests list, call / WhatsApp buttons and one-click “Create booking”.
  • New: trip add-ons customers can tick (roof carrier, pet-friendly cab, child seat…), priced on the server and added to tax, checkout and the booking.
  • New: driver night allowance per night, waiting charges shown before booking, and “Tolls extra / included” on every result card.
  • New: hourly rental packages (km per hour and minimum hours).
  • New: your logo and business name in the sign-up popup, and working Terms, Cancellation and Privacy links (they pointed nowhere before).
  • New: simpler admin menu with 7 entries; related screens are tabs (Fleet & Prices: vehicles, prices, models, brands, categories, service areas).
  • New: plugin can be activated before WooCommerce; the wizard installs it.
  • New: optional “Delete all data when the plugin is deleted” setting and a proper uninstall routine.
  • Changed: plugin name on WordPress.org is now “Outstation – Taxi & Cab Booking for WooCommerce”.
  • Fixed: My Bookings showed a made-up “4.7 (811 ratings)” and “AC” on every car.
  • Fixed: phone number fields always showed +91; they now use your country code.

1.8

  • New: New Booking screen for phone, WhatsApp and walk-in bookings, priced by the same fare engine as the website.
  • New: round trips can be billed for a minimum km per day plus a driver allowance per day (Settings > Payments & Fares; off by default).
  • New: WhatsApp “Chat with us” button (Settings > Booking) and WhatsApp buttons on the Bookings screen that send the trip details to the driver or the customer.
  • New: Trip reminder email the day before pickup, with the driver details (Email Templates > Automatic emails).
  • New: Export bookings to CSV.
  • New: personal data export and erase for customers (Tools > Export / Erase Personal Data) and suggested privacy policy text.
  • New: TaxiService structured data on the home, city, airport and route pages.
  • Fixed: choosing a round trip on the results page showed a one-way fare on the cab details page.

1.7

  • New design: travel-booking look across all customer pages and the admin (brand blue, white cards, orange action buttons, mobile-friendly result cards). Brand and button colours are in Settings > Styling.
  • New: City & Route Pages manager (replaces Content Generator): tabs for cities, airports and routes, search, edit SEO text, show/hide, delete, and add several routes at once.
  • New: Email Templates screen with “Automatic emails”: pick the template for each event (booking confirmed, driver assigned, booking cancelled, new account), switch any email off, preview with sample data and send a test to any address.
  • New: redesigned emails (booking confirmation with fare breakdown, driver trip sheet, cancellation, welcome) wrapped in a branded layout with your logo, colours and support contact.
  • Fixed: editing a default email template was undone on the next page load.
  • New: plugin logo in the admin menu and on the dashboard.
  • New: Support and Rate links on the Plugins screen and a dismissible feedback card on the dashboard.
  • New: Live Preview on WordPress.org with demo cars, routes, cities and airports.
  • Fixed: a pickup time of 10:00 AM chosen by the customer was replaced with “now + 2 hours” on the results and booking pages.
  • Fixed: the Weekly Bookings chart on the dashboard showed numbers but no bars.
  • Fixed: the Settings page jumped down on load; Processing and On-hold bookings now have status badges.
  • Fixed: SMTP on port 465 failed because TLS was always forced; encryption is now chosen automatically (or set it in Settings > Notifications), and emails use your SMTP “From” address.
  • New: Settings are organised in tabs (Booking, Payments & Fares, Notifications, Integrations, Appearance).
  • New: Pages & SEO screen to manage the customer pages: sections on/off, headings and intro text with placeholders, extra FAQs.
  • New: city, airport and route pages use the same pre-filled search widget as the home page.
  • Fixed: the booking form closed one HTML element too many, which broke page layouts inside some templates.
  • Fixed: another company name appeared in the booking page text; it now shows your site name.
  • New: route, city and airport links above the footer on every page (Settings > Styling to turn off).
  • New: airport pages show real airport transfers (distances from the airport) and every page has an FAQ with Google FAQ markup.
  • New: /city-taxi/, /airport-cab/ and /route-carreview/ list every city, airport and route you create, with a search box and booking widget.
  • Security: fares are now always calculated on the server; amounts sent by the browser are ignored at checkout.
  • Security: driver licence/Aadhaar and vehicle RC, insurance and owner ID documents are stored privately and only admins can view them.
  • Security: booking products are hidden from the shop, search and sitemaps, and abandoned ones are cleaned up daily.
  • New: one fare engine for all pages using your Groups pricing (base fare, base km, minimum fare, night charge), plus settings for advance %, convenience fee, discount and tolls.
  • New: setup checklist on the dashboard with one-click page creation, permalinks and classic checkout.
  • New: Astra theme compatibility (full-width booking pages, Login button in the header menu).
  • New: city, airport and route pages share one layout and link to related pages automatically.
  • Fixed: vehicles disappeared from search after one booking; availability is now checked per date.
  • Fixed: round trips were saved as one-way; AC cars were shown as Non-AC.
  • Fixed: customers appeared logged out right after signing in.
  • Privacy: Aadhaar numbers are masked in the drivers list.
  • Fixed: uploads failing on Windows servers, mobile layout overflow, theme header missing on plugin pages, and many smaller bugs.
  • Improved: admin dashboard, Content Generator cards and Settings page are easier to use and work on phones.

1.6

  • Security hardening and localization fixes.
  • Added missing translators comments.
  • Fixed output escaping issues.

1.0

  • Initial release.

short_description: Taxi and cab booking for WordPress: outstation one-way and round trips, airport transfers, hourly rentals, online payment, drivers and SEO city pages.
description:
Outstation turns your WordPress site into a complete taxi and cab booking website, like the big travel apps: outstation one-way and round trips, airport transfers, hourly rentals and city taxis. Customers search, compare cabs with real fares, pay online with any WooCommerce payment gateway and manage their trips. You run cars, drivers, prices, bookings and SEO pages from one simple admin.

Built for taxi operators, travel agencies and car rental companies in any country. Mobile-first, works with any theme (best with Astra, also with block themes such as Twenty Twenty-Five).

For your customers

  • Search like a travel app: one-way, round trip, airport transfer and hourly rental, with stops, date and time pickers and Google address search.
  • Phone address picker: full screen, with “Use current location”, recent places, your own cities and airports, and a map pin for the exact pickup point (the driver gets a navigation link to it).
  • Results with real fares: car photo, fuel, seats, AC, taxes and tolls shown clearly; sort and filter by price, car type and fuel.
  • Review and pay in two app-style steps: itinerary, what is included, extra charges and traveller details, with part pay or full pay.
  • Any WooCommerce payment gateway: Stripe, PayPal, Razorpay, PayU, Cashfree, cash and more.
  • Pay the balance later: pay the rest online from My trips or from a link sent by you or the driver, or pay the driver in cash.
  • My trips: sign in or sign up popup with your logo, upcoming and past trips, trip codes, driver details, payment history, invoices and cancellation. Guests find a booking with its ID and phone.
  • Help and complaints: one support chat per booking, with email notifications on both sides.
  • Genuine reviews: a “Rate your trip” email after the trip; approved reviews show on city and route pages with star ratings for Google.
  • Extras: trip add-ons (roof carrier, child seat…), booking window and minimum notice, whole-amount fares, a callback form and an optional “Call me back” button.

For you and your team

  • Setup wizard: installs WooCommerce and Astra, sets currency, tax and phone code for your country, adds your logo and creates all pages, the menu and sample cars.
  • Bookings: filter by date and status, search, CSV export, phone and WhatsApp bookings with the fare calculated for you, and edit any booking.
  • Booking detail screen: Google Maps links, call and WhatsApp buttons, ready WhatsApp messages, payment link, payment history, trip codes, timeline, and change the car, the driver or both with a reason.
  • Driver app on the phone: a full-screen page with Trips, History and Profile. Drivers sign in with email or mobile and password (emailed when you add them), navigate, call the customer, send a payment link, and start and end the trip with the customer’s codes.
  • Trip codes (OTP): a start code and an end code, so no trip is marked done without the customer.
  • Auto-assign (optional): a free car and driver for each new booking; no car or driver gets two trips at once.
  • No double bookings: a car is busy for every day of its trip, checked again at checkout.
  • Fleet: cars, models, brands, categories, price groups and service areas drawn on the map; one card per model (“Dzire or similar”).
  • Customers, reports and staff: customer history and “Log in as customer”, trips and money per driver and per car, and staff logins (Cab Manager, Dispatcher) that see only what they need.
  • Automatic emails: booking confirmed, driver assigned, cancelled, welcome and reminder, with your branding, preview and test.
  • Invoices: tax invoices with your tax name and number (GST, VAT…); print or save as PDF.

Fares and pricing

  • One server-side fare engine for search, cab page and checkout; prices sent by the browser are never trusted.
  • Base fare, base km, rate per km (AC / non-AC), minimum fare and night charge per car type and fuel.
  • Round trips with minimum km and driver allowance per day; hourly rentals with km per hour and minimum hours.
  • Tax with your own name and rate, convenience fee, online discount, waiting charges, tolls included or extra.

Google Maps, with a small bill

  • Key check: paste your key and see which Google APIs work and which to enable, with a step-by-step guide.
  • Switches for address suggestions, “Use current location”, the map pin and traffic-aware distances. Fares work with all of them off.
  • Fewer paid requests: suggestions after 3 letters and a pause in typing, nothing paid twice in a visit, and server-side caching of every address and distance.
  • An optional server key, so the key in your pages can be locked to your website.

SEO pages that bring bookings

  • City taxi, airport cab and route pages (such as “Bhopal to Indore cab”) with fares for every car, FAQ and structured data.
  • Canonical URLs, meta descriptions, Open Graph tags, breadcrumbs and a sitemap (works with Yoast SEO and Rank Math).
  • Add many routes at once, edit each page’s text, FAQ and sections, and show or hide pages.

Built the WordPress way

  • Every screen is a shortcode on a normal page, so any page builder works around it.
  • Translation-ready, with privacy tools (export and erase personal data) and optional data removal on uninstall.
  • Anonymous usage statistics only if you agree in the setup wizard (see External Services).

Support and custom development

Need help or a custom feature for your cab business? Ask in the support forum or message the developer on WhatsApp: +91 74705 26894.

External Services

The plugin connects to these third-party services:

Google Maps Platform

  • When: the booking form loads Google Maps for address suggestions and the map pin; the server looks up addresses (Geocoding API) and road distances (Routes API or Directions API) to calculate fares; the key check in Settings tests the key when you paste it.
  • Data sent: place names, addresses and map coordinates. No names, phone numbers or emails.
  • Terms · Privacy policy

Razorpay (only if you use it)

  • When: at checkout, when the customer pays with Razorpay.
  • Data sent: order number, amount, currency and the customer’s name, email and phone, to create and verify the payment.
  • Terms · Privacy policy

WordPress.org (setup wizard only)

  • When: only when you click “Install” for WooCommerce or Astra; the standard WordPress download, as in Plugins > Add New. No booking or customer data.
  • Privacy policy

WhatsApp links

  • When: never automatically. Buttons such as “Chat with us” or “WhatsApp driver” open WhatsApp only when clicked, with the message text in the link (trip details, names and phone numbers for admin buttons).
  • Terms · Privacy policy

WP Track by Mapthrust (only if you opt in)

  • When: only if you click “Allow” in the setup wizard or in Settings; “No thanks” works fully, and turning it off deletes your site’s record. Sent on activation, a weekly check-in, update, deactivation (reason only if you give one) and deletion.
  • Data sent: site address and title; plugin, WordPress, PHP, WooCommerce and database versions; language, time zone, country, theme, multisite; server details (web server, PHP limits and extensions, HTTPS, currency); active plugins; which Outstation features are on (never keys); totals of cars, bookings, drivers and service areas, and monthly booking values; and errors in Outstation’s own files.
  • Your email and name only if you also tick the separate updates box (unticked by default). Never passwords, API keys or customer details.
  • Service · Terms and privacy policy

OpenStreetMap Nominatim (admin only)

  • When: only when an administrator clicks “Draw boundary” on the Service areas screen.
  • Data sent: the place name typed in the Location field. No customer data.
  • Usage policy · Privacy policy · Data © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL

Privacy Policy

The plugin stores bookings in your WordPress database: traveller names, phone numbers, emails, pickup and drop locations, dates, times and payment transaction IDs.

  • Locations are sent to Google Maps to calculate distances; payment details go to your payment gateway (see External Services).
  • A customer who rates a trip chooses the name shown with the review; you can hide or delete any review.
  • Cookies: when a customer signs in, signs up or books, a random session cookie (wpcab_user_id) keeps them signed in for 30 days. It holds no personal data. Visitors who only browse get no plugin cookie.
